title: What Character Is It?
synopsis: Test your skills by guessing Chinese riddles!

fullText.simplified:
到底是什么字？

    在中国，人们很喜欢猜谜语。因为猜谜语既可以涨知识，又可以放松。节日的时候，人们会猜灯谜；聚会的时候，人们喜欢猜猜脑筋急转弯或者谜语。
    小张和小王见面聊天，他们聊着聊着就聊到了字谜。
    小张说：“我最近看了几个字谜，考考你吧？”
    小王说：“好哇，我最喜欢猜字谜了。”
    小张说：“听好了！第一个是：清一半，浊一半，打一个字。”
    小王听完，想了想说：“哈哈，我知道了！是蜻蜓的‘蜻’字，对不对？‘清’右半部分的‘青’字和‘浊’右半部分的‘虫’字，加起来就是‘蜻’字！”
    小张说：“不错呀！对了，再听第二个：善一半，恶一半，打一个字。”
    小王摇摇头说：“这个有点儿难，我想想。哎呀，不行啊，想不出来。”
    小张说：“是嗓子哑了的‘哑’字。”他拿出纸和笔，在纸上写了写说：“你看，‘善’下半部分‘口’字加‘恶’上半部分的‘亚’字，加起来就是‘哑’字了。”
    小王说：“这个难，真没想到。还有吗？”
    小张说：“问一半，答一半，一问一答笑半天，打一个字。”
    小王一听就说：“太难了，你告诉我答案吧！”
    小张没说话，只是哈哈大笑。小王一听马上猜出来了。
    朋友们，你知道这个字是什么吗？
    答案是：‘哈’字。你们看，“问”中间的“口”字，加上“答”下半部分的“合”字，加起来就是“哈”字了。你猜对了吗？
fullText.traditional:
到底是什麼字？

    在中國，人們很喜歡猜謎語。因為猜謎語既可以漲知識，又可以放鬆。節日的時候，人們會猜燈謎；聚會的時候，人們喜歡猜猜腦筋急轉彎或者謎語。
    小張和小王見面聊天，他們聊著聊著就聊到了字謎。
    小張說：“我最近看了幾個字謎，考考你吧？”
    小王說：“好哇，我最喜歡猜字謎了。”
    小張說：“聽好了！第一個是：清一半，濁一半，打一個字。”
    小王聽完，想了想說：“哈哈，我知道了！是蜻蜓的‘蜻’字，對不對？‘清’右半部分的‘青’字和‘濁’右半部分的‘蟲’字，加起來就是‘蜻’字！”
    小張說：“不錯呀！對了，再聽第二個：善一半，惡一半，打一個字。”
    小王搖搖頭說：“這個有點兒難，我想想。哎呀，不行啊，想不出來。”
    小張說：“是嗓子啞了的‘啞’字。”他拿出紙和筆，在紙上寫了寫說：“你看，‘善’下半部分‘口’字加‘惡’上半部分的‘亞’字，加起來就是‘啞’字了。”
    小王說：“這個難，真沒想到。還有嗎？”
    小張說：“問一半，答一半，一問一答笑半天，打一個字。”
    小王一聽就說：“太難了，你告訴我答案吧！”
    小張沒說話，只是哈哈大笑。小王一聽馬上猜出來了。
    朋友們，你知道這個字是什麼嗎？
    答案是：‘哈’字。你們看，“問”中間的“口”字，加上“答”下半部分的“合”字，加起來就是“哈”字了。你猜對了嗎？

raw.synopsis: Test your skills by guessing Chinese riddles!
sentence_translations: What Character Is It?
In China, people really like guessing riddles.
Because riddles can both expand your knowledge, and also help you relax.
People will guess riddles written on lanterns during festivals, ..
.. and people like to guess brain teasers or riddles when they gather together.
Little Zhang and Little Wang met up for a chat, and character riddles came up in the conversation.
Little Zhang said, “I’ve seen some character riddles recently, how about I test you?”
Little Wang said, “OK, I like guessing character riddles the most.”
Little Zhang said, “Listen carefully! The first one is:
Take one half of ‘qing’ (clear), one half of ‘zhuo’ (muddy), and make a character.”
Little Wang listened, thought about it and said, ..
.. “Haha, I got it! It’s ‘qing’ from ‘qingting’ (dragonfly), isn’t it?
The right part of ‘qing’ (clear) is ‘qing’ (green), and the right part of ‘zhuo’ (muddy) is ‘chong’ (insect), ..
.. add them together and you get the character ‘qing’!”
Little Zhang said, “Not bad! Now, listen again to the next one:
Take one half of ‘shan’ (virtuous), one half of ‘e’ (evil), and make a character.”
Little Wang shook his head and said, ..
.. “This one is a bit hard. Let me think about it. No, I can’t think of anything.”
Little Zhang said, “It’s ‘ya’ (mute) in the expression ‘sangzi ya’ (to lose one’s voice).”
He took out a piece of paper and a pen, wrote it on the paper, and said, ..
.. “Have a look, the lower part of ‘shan’ (virtuous) is ‘kou’ (mouth), the upper part of ‘e’ (evil) is ‘ya’ (Asia), ..
.. add them together and you get the character ‘ya’ (mute).”
Little Wang said, “This one was hard, I’d never have guessed it. Do you have more?”
Little Zhang said, “Take one half of ‘wen’ (to ask) and one half of ‘da’ (to answer).
One asks, the other answers, and they laugh for a long time. Make a character.”
When he heard this, Little Wang said, “That’s too hard. Tell me the answer!”
Little Zhang didn’t say anything, he just burst out laughing.
When he heard this, Little Wang instantly guessed the answer.
Friends, do you know what the character is?
The answer is “ha” (ha, the sound of laughter).
You see, if you take “kou” (mouth) in the middle of “wen” (to ask), ..
.. and add the lower part of “da” (to answer) which is “he” (to combine), ..
.. add them together and you get the character “ha”. Did you guess right?
